Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 503s and token latency — ThriveWell production

Hi Mina,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 503/504 errors and very high token-latency this morning in our US-West production cluster after the 02:00 UTC model swap. 95th percentile token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and request error rate climbed to ~4.8% for our core inference routes. Throughput dropped ~35% for 30+ minutes and our user-facing queue logs show repeated "quota_exceeded" / "burst_window_exhausted" traces.

Attached is a short sample log (thrivewell_503_sample.log) and a screenshot of our Grafana alert. Can you confirm whether any rate-limiting or quota change was rolled out on your side this morning? This is impacting our latest morning cohort and we need an immediate action plan.

We're available for a quick call — Priya and I can jump now. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Carlos Ramos
Head of Platform Reliability
ThriveWell Health

Subject: INTERNAL: ThriveWell urgent — rate/ burst policy likely culprit (logs attached)

Folks — forwarding Carlos's note and logs. Quick summary after initial look (Connor & Karthik, can you confirm with telemetry):

Findings so far (prelim):
- The customer saw an error spike coincident with this morning's model variant swap (02:00 UTC). Our rollout included a policy sync that inadvertently applied a new burst-window of 10s (was 60s) for the global tenant rate policy in the us-west shard.
- Evidence: quota-policy-diff.png shows the diff between the active and intended policy. KC metrics show the token-bucket drained and the safety-valve kicked in at 02:05 UTC.
- There is a secondary symptom of token leak where continuous-batching behavior for the swapped variant increased per-request token usage by ~15%, which accelerated budget exhaustion.

Suggested immediate actions (minutes-hours):
1) Temporary override: increase ThriveWell's burst window back to 60s and add +30% burst credits. Low risk; reversible. (Connor: please implement and confirm.)
2) Short-term rollback: where safe, rollback the policy sync that changed the burst-window. (Karthik: coordinate with policy service.)
3) Customer comms: Mina to send a short mitigation note and confirm a credit/waiver offer. (Marissa: can you approve up to 10% usage credit for this week? Exec note may be needed.)
4) Postmortem plan: full RCA + test for policy rollout guardrails — add canary check around per-tenant burst-window diffs before global sync. (Owners: SRE + Policy team.)

I'll be on the call in 5. Connor, pls include the remediation steps you intend to run in the call notes. Marissa, looping you for exec-level signoff on credits and whether we should proactively route to our customer success LP.

Thanks,
Mina

Subject: Re: Spike in 503s and token latency — ThriveWell production

Carlos / Priya —

TL;DR: We implemented a temporary burst-window override and throttling credits at 23:10 UTC on 2028-06-21 which immediately brought error rate back under 0.5% and 95th token latency back to ~180ms. Full RCA and permanent fix timeline below.

What happened (short):
- During the scheduled model variant swap (02:00 UTC) a policy-sync job incorrectly applied a reduced burst-window (10s) to the tenant policy in us-west. This, combined with a slight token-size increase for the new variant, caused the token-bucket to exhaust quickly and the safety valve to suppress requests (manifesting as 503s).

What we did (immediate mitigation):
- Applied a conservative override (burst-window -> 60s) + +30% burst credits for ThriveWell at 23:10 UTC (actioned by Connor).
- Rolled back the offending policy-sync and added a temporary canary to block global policy diffs until we validate.
- Replayed sample requests and validated error-rate and latency returned to acceptable levels.

Planned follow-up (timeline):
- 24h: full telemetry capture + token-size profiling across variants (SRE)
- 72h: policy rollout guardrail PR + automated diff canary (Policy team / Karthik)
- 7 days: RCA and customer-facing postmortem with remediation checklist

Credits & exec note: Marissa is looped in for visibility. We're proposing a usage credit equivalent to 8% of this week's bill as a goodwill gesture; Marissa, please confirm offline and we'll include in the postmortem.

Next steps for you:
- Confirm if you'd like an executive-level sync with Marissa and me in the next 24 hours.
- We'll share the RCA draft within 7 days.

Sorry again for the disruption — we take this seriously and are making changes to reduce rollout risk.

Regards,
Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference
